question:
A 59-year-old male with a history of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to polycystic kidney
disease underwent a deceased donor kidney transplant three months ago after four years on
hemodialysis. He had secondary hyperparathyroidism prior to the transplant, with a parathyroid
hormone (PTH) level of 390 pg/ml (normal 10-80 pg/ml). His post-transplant course has been
uneventful, and his current medications include tacrolimus 2 mg twice daily, mycophenolic acid (MPA)
720 mg twice daily, prednisone 5 mg daily, metoprolol 25 mg daily, and calcium with vitamin D
supplements. Laboratory results today show serum creatinine 0.9 mg/dl, sodium 138 mEq/L (normal
135-145 mEq/L), potassium 4.2 mEq/L (normal 3.5-5.2 mEq/L), calcium 8.9 mg/dl (normal 8.5-10.2
mg/dl), phosphorus 2.1 mg/dl (normal 2.5-4.5 mg/dl), and magnesium 1.0 mEq/L (normal 1.8-2 mEq/L).
His vitamin D level was normal last week, and his current PTH level is 450 pg/ml. What is the most
appropriate management for his hyperparathyroidism? Answer Choices: (A) Increase calcium
supplementation (B) Increase vitamin D supplementation (C) Switch to cyclosporine (D) Start
phosphate binders (E) Manage hypomagnesemia aggressively. (F) Reduce tacrolimus dose (G)
Monitor without intervention (H) Refer to endocrine surgeon for possible need of parathyroidectomy. (I)
Start denosumab (J) Start cinacalcet.
 A. Switch to cyclosporine
B. Start denosumab
C. Increase vitamin D supplementation
D. Start cinacalcet.
E. Manage hypomagnesemia aggressively.
F. Reduce tacrolimus dose
G. Monitor without intervention
H. Increase calcium supplementation
I. Refer to endocrine surgeon for possible need of parathyroidectomy.
J. Start phosphate binders
